newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds France late to transpose EU directives.
newsitem.headline: Court finds France late to transpose EU directives.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found on Thursday France failed to implement EU directives on dangerous substances and telecommunications within the time required.
In three separate judgments against France for failing to adopt EU laws, the court reiterated its strict application of implementation time period requirements.

application for a declaration that, by failing to adopt within the periods prescribed the laws, regulations and administrative measures necessary to comply with Council directive 91/157/EEC on dangerous substances and Council directive 93/86/EEC on technical progress the French Republic has failed to comply with its obligations under those directives

1. Declares that, by failing to adopt within the periods prescribed the laws, regulations and administrative measures necessary to comply with Council directive 91/157/EEC on dangerous substances and Council directive 93/86/EEC on technical progress the French Republic has failed to comply with its obligations under those directives
2. Orders the French Republic to pay the costs.
